title: Flat ascent and etale descent for Koszul-regular immersions
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be an immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. An immersion is Koszul-regular if locally at each source point it is a closed immersion into an open subscheme of its target, with ideal locally generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]; the empty sequence is allowed. (1) If $i$ is Koszul-regular and $q:X\prime\to X$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], then the base change $Z\times_X X\prime\to X\prime$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is Koszul-regular. (2) If $(q_a:X_a\to X)_{a\in A}$ is a set-indexed family of etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism] whose images cover $X$, then $i$ is Koszul-regular if and only if all the base changes $Z\times_X X_a\to X_a$ are Koszul-regular. The empty covering of the empty scheme is allowed. No Noetherian, quasi-compactness, separation, or constant-codimension hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0694 (lemma-descending-property-regular-immersion), Koszul-regular clause, restricted to etale covering families; flat ascent is divisors.tex Tag 067P (lemma-flat-base-change-regular-immersion).

proof.text: Prove (1) locally at a point $z\prime$ of the pullback. Factor the immersion as $Z\hookrightarrow V\hookrightarrow X$ with $V$ open. The base change $Z\times_XX\prime\to X\prime$ is an immersion by immersion base change, so its Koszul regularity is meaningful. At the image $z$ of $z\prime$, the affine criterion gives $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset V$ with $Z\times_XU=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ and $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ for a Koszul-regular sequence. Given any open neighbourhood $O$ of the image of $z\prime$ in $X\prime$, choose an affine neighbourhood $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of that point contained in $O\cap q^{-1}U$. The ring map $A\to C$ is flat: apply the affine relative-flatness criterion to the structure module on $q^{-1}U\to U$ and the affine open $W$; its stalk condition is precisely flatness of $q$, and restriction to these opens does not change stalks. The quotient-base-change lemma identifies the pulled-back closed subscheme on $W$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(C/IC)$. Flat ascent for sequences makes the images of the $f_j$ Koszul-regular, and they generate $IC$ by the definition of the extended ideal. Since $O$ was arbitrary, the affine criterion, applied to the closed immersion of the pullback into $q^{-1}V$, now proves Koszul regularity near $z\prime$. The point was arbitrary, proving (1).

source.place: Tag 067P (lemma-flat-base-change-regular-immersion), Koszul-regular proof via Tag 063G and more-algebra.tex Tag 062H; affine flatness is morphisms.tex Tag 01U4.

proof.text: For the forward implication in (2), each $q_a$ is flat by the definition of etale. Apply (1), already proved, separately to every $q_a$.

For the reverse implication keep $Z\hookrightarrow V\hookrightarrow X$ as above. It suffices, by the affine criterion, to prove local Koszul-regular generation for the ideal $I$ on every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset V$, where $Z\times_XU=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. Base change of the given etale covering is an etale covering of $U$. Its covering sieve admits a finite affine refinement $(W_j\to U)_{1\leq j\leq n}$; membership in the generated sieve gives a factorization of each arrow through some $X_a\times_XU$. Both objects are etale over $U$, so the refinement arrow is etale by composition cancellation. It is flat by the definition of etale. The projection $X_a\times_XU\to X_a$ is an open immersion by open-immersion base change, and the pullback immersion on $X_a\times_XU$ is the restriction of the assumed Koszul-regular immersion on $X_a$ to this open; restricting its local defining neighbourhoods preserves the condition. Applying (1) to the refinement arrow proves that the immersion pulled back to each $W_j$ is Koszul-regular.

source.place: Tag 0694 (lemma-descending-property-regular-immersion), affine descent reduction, with descent.tex Tag 02KP and finite affine refinement of etale coverings.

proof.text: Apply the finite affine etale-cover lemma to $(W_j\to U)$, taking its auxiliary abelian sheaf $F$ to be zero. It gives the affine disjoint union $W=\coprod_jW_j=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and a faithfully flat ring map $A\to B$. The quotient-base-change lemma identifies $Z\times_XW$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B/IB)$. Each component $W_j$ is open in this disjoint union. The Koszul-regular neighbourhoods obtained in the preceding step therefore give Koszul-regular neighbourhoods for this closed immersion at every source point. Applying the principal-neighbourhood clause of the affine criterion on $\operatorname{Spec}B$ says exactly that, for each prime $\mathfrak q\supset IB$, some $B_g$ with $g\notin\mathfrak q$ has $(IB)B_g$ generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence.

source.place: Tag 0694 (lemma-descending-property-regular-immersion), faithfully flat affine reduction; more-algebra.tex Tag 068N input and divisors.tex Tag 063G.

proof.text: The faithfully flat ideal-descent lemma applies to the map $A\to B$ and the ideal $I$ just constructed. For each $\mathfrak p\supset I$, it supplies $h\notin\mathfrak p$ and a Koszul-regular generating sequence for $IA_h$. These neighbourhoods can be shrunk into any prescribed open neighbourhood $O$ of $\mathfrak p$: choose $h\prime\notin\mathfrak p$ with $D(hh\prime)\subseteq O\cap D(h)$; the localization $A_h\to A_{hh\prime}$ is flat, so flat base change keeps the images of the sequence Koszul-regular, and they generate $IA_{hh\prime}$. The principal-neighbourhood criterion therefore identifies these with the required neighbourhoods of the original closed immersion over $U$. Varying $U\subset V$ covers every point of $Z$, so $i$ is Koszul-regular. All arguments allow length-zero sequences. If $Z$ is empty, the defining condition has no source points. If $X$ is empty, so is $Z$, and the empty covering proves the equivalence vacuously. No finite subcover of $X$ was used: the finite refinement was chosen separately on each affine $U$.
